title: Secure AI Agent Infrastructure
description: Reproducible research prototypes addressing one question: can an autonomous agent be trusted with a security decision, and would you know if it could not? Contains an agent verification harness that scores whether each claim in an LLM's output is supported by the documents it retrieved, a per-class smart-contract vulnerability benchmark with audited negative controls, and an LLM audit agent. Results files record measured runs against SHA-256-pinned sources; metrics that the evidence does not support are withheld with a machine-readable reason rather than reported. Version 1.1.0 adds a hash-chained stage trail to the audit agent and an indirect prompt-injection experiment: on 20 SmartBugs contracts a planted comment suppressed 14 of 14 detections by an open code model, comment stripping restored all 14, and a string-constant variant still suppressed 11 of 14. Version 1.1.1 makes the benchmark adapter strip source comments before an LLM is scored, so SmartBugs ground-truth labels cannot reach the model; published results are unchanged.
